prompt: GNU diff expand-tabs encoding error column width treatment
answer:
GNU `diff` treats tab and encoding-error widths as follows:

- `--expand-tabs` (`-t`) expands tabs into spaces so tab-aligned columns remain aligned.
- Tab stops are normally every 8 display/print columns; `--tabsize=NUM` changes this.
- For column calculations, `diff` assumes the output device respects tab stops and displays each character with the width reported by the operating system.
- It assumes **each encoding-error byte occupies one column**.
- This is only a guess: there is no standard width for displayed encoding errors. Some programs use one column per byte, others use two columns, and Emacs may use four.
- Consequently, output containing encoding errors or non-ASCII characters may not line up with the display device, and `--ignore-tab-expansion` (`-E`) analysis may differ from what the device displays.

Sources: [GNU diffutils documentation update](https://lists.libreplanet.org/archive/html/diffutils-devel/2023-07/txtLnL_3AmLXk.txt), [Paul Eggert’s explanation](https://public-inbox.org/bug-gnulib/9946e92b-daca-7c7c-bf8d-ff95897774f3@cs.ucla.edu/), [diff manual](http://odysseus.fi.muni.cz/pub/gnu/old-gnu/Manuals/diffutils/html_mono/diff.html).
